original_target.title: A constant comparison between systematic and random Ising updates
original_target.area: Monte Carlo simulation and update scheduling

full_original_statement: For a finite zero-field ferromagnetic Ising measure $`\pi`$ on an $`n`$-vertex graph, let $`K_v`$ resample the spin at $`v`$ conditionally on all other spins. Set $`P=n^{-1}\sum_vK_v`$ and $`P_\alpha=K_{\alpha(1)}\cdots K_{\alpha(n)}`$ for a permutation $`\alpha`$ of the vertices. For a kernel $`Q`$ define $`t_{\rm mix}(Q)=\min\{t\in\mathbb N:\max_\sigma\|Q^t(\sigma,\cdot)-\pi\|_{\rm TV}\le1/4\}`$. Is there an absolute $`C<\infty`$ such that $`n\,t_{\rm mix}(P_\alpha)\le C\,t_{\rm mix}(P)`$ for every graph, every finite nonnegative set of couplings, and every $`\alpha`$? One step of $`P_\alpha`$ is a complete sweep.
queries: "Ising" "systematic scan" "constant" comparison (site:arxiv.org OR site:zenodo.org OR site:hal.science OR site:github.com)

sources.scope_comparison: The actual comparison loses powers of n and logarithmic stationary-mass factors. Its tight counterexample uses an antiferromagnetic model, so it does not refute the ferromagnetic-only absolute constant. Recent spectral-independence results add high-temperature correlation assumptions. No universal all-couplings ferromagnetic constant comparison found.
